problem:
Given that the differential equation

$$
{t}^{2}{y}^{″}-3t{y}^{′}+3y=2{t}^{4}{e}^{t},\,t>0
$$

has the complimentary function ${y}_{c}(t)=At+B{t}^{3}$, find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(t)$ to this equation.

*Hint: You may wish to make use of the following result:*

$$
\int {t}^{2}{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t=({t}^{2}-2t+2){e}^{t}+C
$$
worked_solution:
First, we reduce the differential equation to the form

$$
{y}^{″}+P(t){y}^{′}+Q(t)y=f(t).
$$

So, we divide both sides of the given equation by ${t}^{2}.$ We get

$$
{y}^{″}-\frac{3}{t}{y}^{′}+\frac{3}{{t}^{2}}y=2{t}^{2}{e}^{t}.
$$

We notice that the forcing term $f(t)=2{t}^{2}{e}^{t}.$ Additionally, we're given the fundamental solutions:

$$
{y}_{1}(t)=t,\,{y}_{2}(t)={t}^{3}
$$

First, let's compute the Wronskian:

$$
\begin{aligned}W({y}_{1},{y}_{2}) & =|\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & {y}_{2} \\ {y}_{1}^{′} & {y}_{2}^{′}\end{aligned}| \\  & ={y}_{1}{y}_{2}^{′}-{y}_{1}^{′}{y}_{2} \\  & =(t)({t}^{3})^{′}-{(t)}^{′}({t}^{3}) \\  & =3{t}^{3}-{t}^{3} \\  & =2{t}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the Wronskian is not equal to zero, this confirms that the functions ${y}_{1}(t)$ and ${y}_{2}(t)$ are independent.

According to the method of variation of parameters, the particular solution of the differential equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}(t) & ={y}_{1}(t)u(t)+{y}_{2}(t)v(t),\end{aligned}
$$

where

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =-\int \frac{f(t){y}_{2}(t)}{W({y}_{1},{y}_{2})}\,\text{d}t=-\int {t}^{2}{e}^{t}=-({t}^{2}-2t+2){e}^{t}, \\ v(t) & =\int \frac{f(t){y}_{1}(t)}{W({y}_{1},{y}_{2})}\,\text{d}t=\int {e}^{t}={e}^{t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}(t) & ={y}_{1}(t)u(t)+{y}_{2}(t)v(t) \\  & =-t({t}^{2}-2t+2){e}^{t}+{t}^{3}{e}^{t} \\  & =(2{t}^{2}-2t){e}^{t}.\end{aligned}
$$
